meta.layering_note: engineering_fact = what the API/link docs literally say. program_policy = Operating Agreement or Program Policies. policy_risk = an ambiguity or exposure, NOT a legal opinion. Tawveeri's governing documents are the amazon.sa Agreement and Policies. The amazon.com text is cited where it is newer or clearer and may not be identical to the .sa text.

items.engineering_fact: The Creators API is the only documented programmatic source of Amazon price and availability data. Prices come through OffersV2: the migration guide marks legacy Offers as 'Not Available. use OffersV2'. Program text sets the API display mechanics. A date/time stamp must sit next to the price unless the data is refreshed at least hourly. Non-image content may be cached for up to 24 hours and must then be refreshed through the API. Images may not be cached; only image links may be stored, for up to 24 hours. ASINs may be stored indefinitely. Amazon publishes no documented API or format for showing prices taken by scraping.
items.program_policy: There are only two permitted sources for a site's Amazon prices and availability. Either (a) Amazon serves the link that shows the price, or (b) the site gets the data through the Creators API or PA API and follows that API's rules. When the stamp is required, the price must carry an 'as of' date/time, e.g. 'Amazon.com Price: $32.77 (as of 01/07/2008 14:11 PST- Details)'. The site must also show the disclaimer that prices and availability are accurate as of the date/time shown and may change, and that the price on Amazon at purchase time applies. Stale data: anything cached longer than 24 hours must be refreshed immediately or not displayed. Scraping: the license expressly excludes 'data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools'. Program Content may not be altered. The amazon.sa Arabic policies contain the same two-source rule, naming PA-API, plus the 'as of' stamp and the 24-hour cache limit.
items.policy_risk: HIGH. Showing Amazon.sa prices scraped from search or product pages is outside both permitted sources. The license also expressly excludes robots and data-extraction tools, so this is not a grey area in the text. Adding 'as of' timestamps does not cure the sourcing problem, because the timestamp rule is a condition attached to API-sourced data. One ambiguity remains: the .sa Arabic policy names only PA-API, which is now retired, while the .com policy (April 2026) names Creators API or PA API. Whether the .sa text is simply outdated is unconfirmed.

items.engineering_fact: Amazon's documented simple text link is 'http://www.amazon.com/dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag=YOURASSOCIATEID', and Amazon says this format qualifies for the direct link bonus. The tag is a URL parameter in the form XXXXX-## (for example tawveeri0f-21). No current official page found makes linkCode mandatory. linkCode appears in Amazon-generated links and older docs, but no rule was found that requires or forbids it. Sub-tags, i.e. additional tracking IDs, are issued by Amazon and placed in the URL.
items.program_policy: Special Links must use your assigned Associates ID, and the tag must appear as a parameter in every link to an Amazon Site. Several rules govern redirects and cloaking. A 'Redirecting Link' sends users to Amazon through an intermediate site without a click or other affirmative action there. Purchases through such links are Disqualified (no commission). You may not cloak, hide or spoof your site's URL or user agent so that Amazon cannot tell where a click came from. Link shorteners or buttons may not hide that the destination is Amazon. Sub-tags may be used to measure the performance of different Special Links. They may NOT be assigned dynamically to individual users to track their behaviour. Bots: you may not 'artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise'. The .sa Arabic policy has the equivalent rule. Incentivised clicks and self-purchases are prohibited. The .sa Agreement §1 defines Special Links ('الروابط المخصصة') as links that properly use the tagged formats Amazon provides.
items.policy_risk: MEDIUM. A human clicking a visible 'Go to Amazon' button that hits /go and gets a 302 to amazon.sa has taken an affirmative action on Tawveeri, so it does not clearly meet the 'Redirecting Link' definition. Neither the Agreement nor the Policies explicitly allows or forbids a server-side click-tracking hop, so this is ambiguous. Three conditions reduce the risk: the visible UI must make clear the user is going to Amazon; the redirect must not mask the referring site or user agent; and the final URL must carry the tag unaltered. Bot exposure is the larger risk. Any crawler that follows /go to amazon.sa with the tag creates sessions Amazon could treat as 'artificially generated ... by way of a robot', whether or not you intended them. Dynamically assigning ascsubtag/sub-tags per user or session is expressly prohibited. Assigning per placement or per page type is allowed.

items.engineering_fact: None (there is no technical requirement; this is purely a policy matter).
items.program_policy: The .sa Operating Agreement §5 (last updated 2026-01-05) requires the site to 'clearly and prominently' display the statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases', or a substantially similar statement previously allowed. The official Arabic wording is 'بصفتي مشارك لأمازون ، فإنني أكسب من عمليات الشراء المؤهلة.' The .com §5 has the same requirement. The Policies separately require accurate disclosure of cookies and pixels, through a privacy policy or otherwise, and compliance with applicable law. The 'as of' price disclaimer from Q1 is a separate disclosure that applies to API-sourced prices.
items.policy_risk: LOW-MEDIUM. Neither document fixes a placement such as every page or next to each link. The only placement standard is 'clearly and prominently ... on your Site'. A footer-only or terms-only disclosure is a judgment call. Saudi consumer and advertising law may add requirements beyond Amazon's; that question is not assessed here.

items.engineering_fact: STATUS: PA-API 5 is deprecated. Calls now return HTTP 403 'Product Advertising API is deprecated. Please migrate to Creators API.' The legacy webservices.amazon.com/paapi5 docs URLs now 302 to the deprecation notice. A third-party article (not official) gives the dates as 30 April 2026 for deprecation and 15 May 2026 for endpoint retirement. SAUDI SUPPORT: yes. The Creators API locale reference has an SA page: marketplace value 'www.amazon.sa', languages en_AE and ar_AE, currency SAR. affiliate-program.amazon.sa/creatorsapi exists behind an amazon.sa Associates login (it redirects to signin with assoc_handle=amzn_associates_sa). MIGRATION: OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow (Credential ID + Secret + Version); Bearer token valid for 1 hour; endpoint creatorsapi.amazon/catalog/v1/...; lowerCamelCase parameters (partnerTag, itemIds); x-marketplace header; up to 10 item IDs per GetItems call; prices through OffersV2 only.
items.program_policy: ELIGIBILITY: the applicant must be a registered, valid Amazon Associate in the target marketplace and must 'Have at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days to access the PA API through the Creators API'. Credentials are created in Associates Central under Tools > Creators API, and each marketplace needs its own Associate registration and partner tag. The official FAQ says credentials 'work globally' but need valid Partner Tags and regional approval. A third-party source (not official) reports that access is suspended if the account falls below 10 sales in 30 days and restored once the threshold is met again. The Creators API license and the Program Policies' Usage Requirements govern display: the timestamp, 24-hour cache and no-image-cache rules, and a ban on use in seller tools or for ML training.
items.policy_risk: Migration is gated on commercial performance, not on engineering. The tawveeri0f-21 amazon.sa account needs 10 qualifying (shipped) sales in a rolling 30 days. Until it reaches that, the only compliant way to show Amazon prices is (a) in Q1, i.e. Amazon-served links. This creates a chicken-and-egg problem: the sales that unlock the API must come from link-only (price-less) placements. Whether the .sa program still enforces exactly the .com threshold was not confirmed from an .sa-specific public page, because the .sa Creators API pages are behind login.

items.engineering_fact: The documented canonical link is /dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag=... (see Q2). No official Amazon page found mentions sponsored-ad click URLs (/sspa/click, aax, etc.) as a Special Link format.
items.program_policy: Product-list pages are allowed as link destinations, with a condition. The Policies say 'Product lists include search results, events (e.g. Prime Day), or a department homepage', and 'When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link.' No Amazon rule found addresses sponsored-ad click URLs.
items.policy_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH for /sspa/click URLs. They are Amazon Ads click-tracking endpoints, not Special Link formats Amazon provides. Routing affiliate traffic through them may register advertiser ad clicks that Amazon could treat as artificially generated clicks or sessions. It may also break attribution or count as altering Program Content. Inference only: there is no explicit rule, but it is not a sanctioned format. Search-result URLs are permitted only with relevant original content. A comparison page that maps a specific product to Amazon should use /dp/ASIN?tag=... (the documented, bonus-eligible format) rather than a search URL.

evidence.quote: Product lists include search results, events (e.g. Prime Day), or a department homepage (e.g. grocery).
When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link.

items.engineering_fact: No API feature specific to comparison sites was found. OffersV2 in the Creators API is the documented route to Amazon offer and price data.
items.program_policy: Comparison sites are explicitly contemplated and allowed, with a display obligation. If you show Amazon prices in any 'comparison' format, including a price-comparison tool or engine, next to other sites' prices, you must show the lowest 'new' price and, if Amazon provides it, the lowest 'used' price on the Amazon Site. The .sa Arabic policy has the same clause. All Q1 sourcing rules still apply: prices must come from Amazon-served links or the API.
items.policy_risk: HIGH while prices are scraped. A comparison engine is permitted, but the comparison clause assumes prices that are legitimately sourced and then adds the lowest-new (and lowest-used) obligation on top. A scraped single-offer price, such as a buy-box or search-tile price, may also fail to be the 'lowest new' price.

evidence.quote: if you choose to display prices for any Product on your Site in any 'comparison' format (including through the use of any price-comparison tool or engine) together with prices for the same or similar products offered through any web site or other means other than an Amazon Site, you must display both the lowest 'new' price and, if we provide it to you, the lowest 'used' price at which the Product is available on the Amazon Site.
